STEP 1 - Scene: A salad of mixed leafy greens (looks like mixed lettuce/mesclun with red-stemmed leaves such as chard or beet greens) with walnut pieces and a few black olives, served on a large white square plate. Photographed from above (near top-down view), so the plate is seen roughly undistorted.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white plate is square-ish, roughly 27 cm across its width. Using a diameter-equivalent of ~27 cm: area = 3.14 x (13.5)^2 ≈ 572 cm^2. The plate is square, so the actual area is closer to 27 x 27 ≈ 729 cm^2; I use the ~600 cm^2 working area for the round-equivalent estimate.

STEP 3 - Items: mixed leafy greens (lettuce and red-stemmed greens), walnut pieces (about 3), black olives (2), a light dressing sheen possibly present on the leaves.

STEP 4 - Area: Greens cover about 12% of the plate, walnuts about 1%, olives about 0.5%. Total food coverage ~13% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Greens cover ~80 cm^2 at a loose height of ~4 cm = ~320 ml. Walnuts: 3 pieces, ~2 cm^3 each = ~6 ml. Olives: 2 pieces, ~4 ml each = ~8 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Greens 320 ml x 0.15 = 48 g. Walnuts 6 ml x 0.5 (dense nut pieces, roughly 0.5-0.6 g/ml) ≈ 4 g. Olives 8 ml x 0.9 ≈ 7 g. Dressing is not clearly visible, so none is added.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Mixed leafy greens: 48 g x 20 kcal/100 g ≈ 10 kcal
- Walnuts: 4 g x 654 kcal/100 g ≈ 26 kcal
- Black olives: 7 g x 115 kcal/100 g ≈ 8 kcal
Total ≈ 44 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total of ~59 g is plausible for a small side salad that covers only about an eighth of a large plate. A modest dressing would add some energy, but none is clearly visible, so it is excluded.
